transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We need to address an urgent issue before tomorrow's day shift. The overhead crane above the fabrication area has a cracked mounting bracket that must be repaired by welding before we can proceed with any high-load lifts. Since steel frame production is scheduled for tomorrow, we need to get this repair done today. This crane repair is classified as hot work, so I need to convene a pre-job review with maintenance and EHS to check the work scope, production impact, and safety controls before I can issue the hot-work authorization. Ravi and Monique, I'll need each of you to enter your reviewed findings into the formal review record before I close the pre-job review. Once all controls are in place and the authorization is filed, welding can begin. Can we start that review now?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should share my engineering assessment during this review. My assessment specifies that the bracket repair requires exactly 4 hours of crane lockout and fabrication-area stoppage. I completed the assessment from the repair contractor's work package yesterday, but I should note that the maintenance work order still shows only an unconfirmed duration.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my permit review findings during this pre-job review. My review specifies that this weld location requires a two-person fire watch, atmospheric testing every 2 hours, and a 15-meter exclusion boundary for combustible materials. I confirmed these requirements against the site's hot-work standard this morning, but I should note that the permit draft has not yet been filed.
